project.name: PyNext experimental Python + Rust framework
project.audience: Python developers evaluating an experimental framework
project.goal: Understand current supported routing, read a genuine example, reach docs or source

identitySignals.signal: PyNext combines a Python page-authoring surface with a Rust Axum routing engine
identitySignals.source: Current PyNext README description of Python and Rust layers
identitySignals.designDecision: Show a real Python route and labeled routing stages instead of a decorative SaaS screen

identitySignals.signal: The project's primary proof is a minimal documented Python page example
identitySignals.designDecision: Place actual supported Python syntax before features or marketing cards

identitySignals.signal: PyNext clearly describes experimental limitations and operating boundaries
identitySignals.source: PyNext README experimental and security caveats
identitySignals.designDecision: Use an honest experimental status and limitation notes, not production-grade marketing claims

directions.name: Runtime Blueprint
directions.thesis: Show Python authoring and Rust routing as one legible, documented architectural story
directions.narrative: First: Python-facing pages and Rust routing. Then: a verified route example and a source-backed request path.
directions.heroLayout: Asymmetric two-column hero: Python route snippet left, carefully labeled runtime path right, CTA below the thesis
directions.motif: Functional route-path strokes connect valid handler and architecture details across hero and docs sections
directions.proof: Actual Python @page example and a diagram whose labels must be verified against repository docs
directions.risk: Diagram may crowd the hero or imply unsupported stability at mobile sizes
directions.responsive390: Stack thesis and CTA first, then scrollable selectable Python snippet, followed by diagram with text labels

typography.display: Humanist system sans with compact medium-weight technical editorial headings
typography.body: Highly readable sans text optimized for precise architecture explanations
typography.code: System monospace code with distinct syntax, valid indentation and a readable gutter

cta.primary: Open the actual current PyNext quickstart documentation
cta.secondary: View the upstream PyNext source repository

evidence.reference: PyNext GitHub README describes Python pages and Rust Axum routing with experimental limitations
evidence.claim: Python pages and API handlers are supported by the experimental framework described in README

contentOutline: First screen: documented Python page alongside the labeled Rust routing flow
Second section: actual route anatomy and source-grounded handler mapping
Third section: quickstart steps, current capabilities and honest limitations

directions.name: The Python Surface
directions.thesis: Make the minimal Python page the hero so the authoring experience is instantly understandable
directions.narrative: Begin with a readable editorial promise and minimal page example, then walk through build and documented capabilities.
directions.heroLayout: Single-column broad editorial headline followed by a large full-width, readable Python implementation block
directions.motif: Syntax-line markers and typographic spacing make the real API page the defining visual signature
directions.proof: Runnable-looking minimal Python page derived from current docs, with constraints clearly stated
directions.risk: Documentation-like presentation may feel familiar rather than uniquely branded
directions.responsive390: One-column editorial headline then horizontally scrollable code with readable font sizes and quickstart CTA

typography.display: High-contrast light editorial sans emphasizing the promise over mechanical decoration
typography.body: Wide-measure readable documentation font with generous paragraph spacing
typography.code: Large highly legible mono with simple code-highlight discipline

cta.primary: Read the real minimal quickstart example
cta.secondary: Browse the project source and architecture files

evidence.reference: PyNext README app example demonstrates the Python h and page API
evidence.claim: Actual supported Python page syntax is an appropriate visual proof of the framework

contentOutline: First screen: editorial Python promise with a large selectable page source example
Second section: walkthrough of minimal authoring and supported page behavior
Third section: integration details, limits and documentation links

directions.name: Builder's Field Notes
directions.thesis: Earn trust through transparent engineering notes about what the framework currently does and does not support
directions.narrative: Lead with the honest experimental motivation, then show working capabilities and limitations before the example.
directions.heroLayout: Editorial notebook column with annotated side-notes and a concise capability status rail beside the introduction
directions.motif: Source-backed annotation margin and version notes recur as a structured engineering journal pattern
directions.proof: Supported feature list and real limitations linked to project docs rather than made-up metrics
directions.risk: Dense content and marginal notes can obscure the quickstart action
directions.responsive390: Convert annotated margin into ordered in-flow footnotes and keep links discoverable

typography.display: Characterful humanist display style with modest hierarchy and visible section numbering
typography.body: Comfortable print-inspired reading font with careful line length and source footnotes
typography.code: Secondary mono accent only for exact source citations and documented commands

cta.primary: Review the current capabilities and limitations
cta.secondary: Open source repository and working examples

evidence.reference: PyNext README explicitly warns about experimental and production limitations
evidence.claim: This is an experimental framework with documented security and operating boundaries

contentOutline: First screen: experimental field note, verified scope and concise author motivation
Second section: supported and unsupported capabilities with source-referenced annotations
Third section: modest quickstart example, roadmap and changelog-style follow-up

decision.why: It gives PyNext a defensible visual metaphor rooted in real Python and Rust architecture while proving the actual page-writing API immediately. This is a design hypothesis, not a tested screenshot winner.

productFit.runtime-blueprint: High because the two runtime layers are central to the product identity
productFit.python-surface: High for the Python-first authoring experience but omits the engine distinction
productFit.builder-notes: Medium because transparency matters but can distract from the framework concept

proofCredibility.runtime-blueprint: High if every Python and Rust label is checked against actual docs
proofCredibility.python-surface: High because the first screen is a real minimal Python source example
proofCredibility.builder-notes: High for true limitations and public source references instead of metrics

distinctiveness.runtime-blueprint: High because the routing-path motif derives from PyNext's engineering architecture
distinctiveness.python-surface: Medium because a code-heavy editorial hero is common in documentation sites
distinctiveness.builder-notes: High because a source-backed engineering notebook has an uncommon structure

readability.runtime-blueprint: Medium given the diagram must be legible and simplified at 390px
readability.python-surface: High because the single-column syntax showcase is easy to scan
readability.builder-notes: Medium given annotation and supporting footnote density

implementationCost.runtime-blueprint: Medium because a correct architecture figure and responsive layout require validation
implementationCost.python-surface: Low because editorial layout and code module are straightforward
implementationCost.builder-notes: Medium because true notes, citations and editorial hierarchy require content curation

losingStrengths.python-surface: Its full-width runnable example is clearer on mobile and cheaper to build
losingStrengths.builder-notes: Its honest capabilities and limitations can establish unusual developer trust

brandDNA.positioning: Experimental Python developer ergonomics supported by a Rust Axum routing engine, with documented current limitations
brandDNA.typography: Humanist system sans headlines and body text paired with system monospace for actual Python code and API fragments
brandDNA.colors: Named ink, muted surface, accessible route-blue signal, focus and error roles; contrast requires real measurement
brandDNA.signatureMotif: A source-grounded file-route path connecting URL and documented Python handler to the Rust routing stage
brandDNA.layoutGrammar: Asymmetric readable code-and-path hero; connected route anatomy and docs modules; 390px stacks text then proof
brandDNA.proofStyle: Real examples from the current PyNext README and docs, never invented popularity or performance statistics
brandDNA.interaction: Route-path highlighting only where it illustrates verified flow, with reduced motion and keyboard behavior
brandDNA.responsive390: Headlines wrap into stacked thesis and CTA; code remains selectable and scrollable, diagram becomes labeled sequence
motifApplications: Use factual path geometry beside the hero code pane
Repeat the same route-path lines in a real quickstart and architecture section
antiTemplates: Reject a generic gradient behind empty SaaS dashboard cards
Reject fabricated GitHub stars and benchmarks
Reject decorative fake terminal outputs or compatibility badges
brandDNA.contentVoice: Documentation-like, experimentally honest and technically precise; avoid generic innovation slogans
brandDNA.signatureContent: Real Python page syntax, source-verified route diagram and transparent experimental boundaries

identityLinks.treatment: Use a verified route-path motif and legible diagram labels
Show selectable current supported Python syntax with genuine quickstart link
State documented limits plainly and make unsupported claims visibly absent

substitutionTest.replacement: A typical React-only SaaS agency developer portfolio with no PyNext runtime

fails.reason: The substituted project has no equivalent documented Python/Axum stages to support the hero diagram

fails.element: Minimal PyNext page snippet and experimental boundary notes
fails.reason: The alternative owner would need different real API examples and different project-specific limitations
